## kb_to_source

The docs were read sentence by sentence. Every obligation, calculation, condition and procedure in them has a structured source, except these:

- continence_balance_shared_need_share: "Continence balance is the running total … **rounded to the cent**". The rule text has no rounding. The compute does round (`cont_balance: RND(…, 2)`), and a sum of two-decimal postings is already at the cent, so this adds no new semantics. Note only.
- convex_barrier_usage_rate case 1 ("Previous refill of 75 units for 90 days … rate … 25 per 30 days") uses the same figures as this task's previous refill (0f46c963, 75/90). It yields only an intermediate. The task's scored units depend on the 7 days left, and the example uses 12, so no scored value is exposed. Note only.
- No cross-problem operational guidance: no doc says "if unmet, first call …". The only tool named in each hub is that hub's own tool.
- No opening world state is written as a policy fact: no document states that a customer has arrears, an approved application, or a late delivery.
- No added confirmation, review or notification steps were found.

### Policy-side note (not a KB verdict)

The generic adjustments sentence the round-3 source puts in every `result` tells a reader of the computation document that adjustments of a given kind exist. Examples are notice "changes to the 30-day blocks and shares added to the excess … units deducted", refill "Extra barriers" defined but not counted in the standard units, and correction "Each service-recovery part". This is the coordinator's XF_recipe item 4 design, and the KB is obliged to carry the source sentence. It names no factor and no record, so it pre-solves no search, but it is weaker than full silence.
